title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - streaming stability, function calls, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Arielle Chen
description: This PR finishes parity work for the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat.completions endpoint: it stabilizes streaming semantics, adds support for function/tool calling (function_call param + inferred signatures), aligns role handling and stop/logprobs behavior with OpenAI, and improves response formatting for structured output and JSON schema-like enforcement. Motivation: customers using the OpenAI compatibility layer reported subtle differences in stream boundaries, tool-call semantics, and logprob/stop handling that caused integration breakage (see ENG-4123, ENG-4190). Changes are intentionally scoped to API surface and routing; model runtime behavior is unchanged except for streaming framing and metadata emitted. Checklist: [x] streaming framing & chunk ordering tests; [x] function_call param passthrough and local function signature inference; [x] roles canonicalization (system/user/assistant/unknown fallback); [x] stop token handling and logprobs propagation; [x] structured output content-type and top-level JSON enforcement; [x] extensive integration tests and nightly e2e matrix. Migration notes: existing clients should see compatible behavior for non-OpenAI params; OpenAI clients using function_call, stop, or requesting logprobs should be able to point to the same endpoint without special routing. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged for Redwood-native routes; the OpenAI compatibility flag is opt-in at the API key / route level. Rollout: staged canary on dedicated clusters with 10% traffic for 48h then 50% then full. Related: ENG-4123, ENG-4190, DOCS-789.
commits: feat(openai-compat): support function_call param and map to internal tool routing
fix(streaming): ensure chunk order and final 'done' sentinel for partial function calls
feat(api): canonicalize role names and add unknown->assistant fallback for legacy messages
feat(stop/logprobs): forward stop tokens to runtime and include logprobs when requested
feat(formatting): add structured_output hinting and Content-Type: application/json in streaming frames
test(openai-compat): add integration tests for streaming + function calls + stops
docs: update openai compatibility guide and migration notes
review_comments: Jordan Patel: Please add an explicit test for partial function calls streaming (function name + partial args) - observed in staging.
Arielle Chen: Added test and updated frame serializer to emit final DONE sentinel for partial tools. See tests/integration/test_function_calls_endtoend.py.
Sofia Martinez: Can we ensure role canonicalization doesn't rewrite user-provided 'assistant' messages? Concerned about auditability.
Arielle Chen: Canonicalization is idempotent and only normalizes casing/aliases; original role is preserved in metadata for auditing.
Kenji Yamamoto: The stop token handling looks good, but please document interaction with prefix caching and batching (it can affect tokenization).
Arielle Chen: Added section to docs/openai-compatibility.md clarifying cache boundaries and recommended stop token usage.
testing_notes: Integration matrix exercised: streaming (chunk order, final sentinel), function_call surface (explicit/auto/infer), stop tokens and logprobs propagation, structured_output enforcement, and SDK compatibility tests (Python/TS). Benchmarks showed <1% tail-latency impact and ~3% throughput drop in degenerate function-call-heavy workloads; we added batching hint to reduce regressions.
merge_summary: Squash-merged after approvals from Jordan, Sofia, and Kenji. No outstanding issues; canary rollout completed and metrics met SLOs. Docs updated and migration notes added to openai-compatibility.md.
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: streaming stability improvements; function_call param support and partial function-call streaming; role canonicalization matching OpenAI semantics; stop token handling and logprobs propagation; improved structured output/JSON framing in streaming responses; docs + SDK examples updated.
